operating_notes.text: Jindal Stainless had FY25 turnover of ₹40,182 crore (USD 4.75 billion) and is ramping facilities to 4.2 million tonnes of annual melt capacity in FY27.
The company had 16 stainless steel manufacturing and processing facilities in India and abroad, including Spain and Indonesia, and a network in 12 countries, as of March 2025.
FY26 consolidated revenue ₹42,955 Cr with EBITDA margin 12.98%, up from 11.76% in FY25.
Net debt rose to ₹6,926 Cr at Mar-2026 from ₹6,104 Cr at Sep-2025; debt/equity 0.37x.
Inventory build of ₹790 Cr in Q4FY26 versus ₹111 Cr in Q3FY26.
FY26 finished goods sales volume 25,65,902 tonnes, up 8.1% YoY.
Q4FY26 standalone sales volume 6,41,743 tonnes, down 0.1% YoY.
Domestic share of total sales 92% in FY26, 95% in Q4FY26.
FY26 standalone sales volume 2,566 thousand MT, up 8% YoY; Q4FY26 642 thousand MT, flat YoY and down 1% QoQ.
Sales composition: domestic 93% of Q4FY26 and 92% of FY26 sales; exports 7% and 8% respectively.
Nickel LME quarterly average fell to USD 17,356/MT in Q4FY26 from USD 22,308/MT in Q1FY24; ferrochrome averaged ₹1,16,800/MT in Q4FY26.
Hisar unit achieved Zero Waste to Landfill certification with Platinum+ rating and a 99.99% waste diversion rate for FY 2024-25.
FY26 annual turnover ₹42,955 Cr (USD 4.86 billion); facilities being ramped to 4.2 MTPA annual melt capacity in FY27.
On-going projects: ~₹1,900 Cr downstream HRAP & CRAP augmentation, ~₹1,200 Cr infrastructure and ESG projects, ~₹710 Cr Indonesia 1.2 MTPA melt shop JV (49%).
Shareholding at 31 March 2026: promoter 62.0%, FII 20.9%, DII 7.2%, retail & others 9.9%.
Consolidated contingent liabilities were ₹717.03 Cr at 31 March 2026, including ₹313.60 Cr excise/GST and ₹162.18 Cr income-tax claims.
Related-party flows totalled ₹4,204.54 Cr in FY26, led by ₹1,054.23 Cr of goods sold to JSL Global Commodities Pte. Ltd.
The Group held a 49% stake in associate PT Cosan Metal Industry with a ₹758.05 Cr receivable at 31 March 2026.
Scrap feed is about 85-90% at Hisar and 70-75% at Jajpur, with 90-95% of scrap sourced domestically and from Southeast Asia and under 2-3% from Europe.
Chromeni ran at 80-85% utilisation and Rathi at about 70%; Chromeni was fully on pipe natural gas during the gas disruption.
Green hydrogen capacity: 90 Nm3/hr installed at Hisar with 200 more in two quarters; 600 Nm3/hr at Jajpur commissioning in August, rising to 1,200 next year, on about ₹35 Cr capex.
Q1FY27 grade mix was 35% 200-series, 47% 300-series and 18% 400-series.
Scrap feed is about 85-90% at Hisar and 70-75% at Jajpur, with 90-95% of scrap sourced domestically and from Southeast Asia.
Chromeni ran at 80-85% utilisation and Rathi at about 70% in Q1FY27; Chromeni ran fully on pipe natural gas during the gas disruption.
FY26 sales volume was 2,566 thousand tonnes and Q1FY27 revenue ₹11,279 Cr, with FY26 EBITDA/t of ₹21,670 and Q1FY27 ₹22,884.
Deck cites ~70-72% scrap utilisation in EAF production and a 70% shift to make-to-anticipation (MTA) cutting lead time by more than one-third.
Debt maturity profile runs ₹786 Cr in FY27, ₹562 Cr FY28, ₹555 Cr FY29, ₹559 Cr FY30, ₹524 Cr FY31 and ₹1,803 Cr FY32 onwards.
JSL Overseas Holding Limited holds 14,43,02,316 shares or 17.50% of Jindal Stainless after buying 8,61,553 shares on 18 and 21 September 2026, with nil encumbrance.
Jindal Stainless redeemed all 990 NCDs of ISIN INE220G07127 at ₹10,00,000 each (₹99 Cr total) on the stated date.
Jindal Stainless deployed 10 electric trucks on Jajpur-Kharagpur-Kolkata routes, alongside 80 LNG trucks and newly begun CNG trucks from Dhamra to Jajpur.
The combined electric, CNG and LNG mix is expected to move 8,000-10,000 tonnes of cargo a month and cut about 71 tonnes CO₂ monthly, around 26% versus diesel.
Green fleet of 10 electric, 80 LNG and CNG trucks plus 60 CNG buses is expected to move 8,000-10,000 tonnes of cargo a month and cut ~71 tonnes CO₂ a month, about 26% versus diesel.
PT Glory Metal Indonesia reclassified from subsidiary to associate effective July 1, 2026.
Settled long-disputed Haryana Entry Tax demands for ₹101.72 Cr in tranches.
Fully redeemed 990 listed secured NCDs of ₹99 Cr in Q2FY27.
Board approved amalgamation of Chromeni Steels, Rabirun Vinimay, JSL Super Steel, and Jindal United Steel into Jindal Stainless.

timeline.summary: On 23 April 2026 Jindal Stainless launched its first brand campaign, 'Jindal Saathi Seal Hai, Toh Asli Stainless Steel Hai', fronted by Ranveer Singh and built around a co-branded authenticity seal for Pipes & Tubes.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹11,337.19 Cr (+11.2% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹843.56 Cr (+42.7% YoY).

On 4 May 2026 Jindal Stainless filed its Q4 & FY26 earnings presentation: consolidated FY26 revenue ₹42,955 Cr (+9% YoY), EBITDA ₹5,560 Cr (+19%), PAT ₹3,185 Cr (+27%), net debt down to ₹3,040 Cr, and a stated plan to reach 4.2 MTPA melt capacity in FY27.
On 5 May 2026, Jindal Stainless reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹11,337 Cr and PAT of ₹834 Cr, and guided for 7-9% volume growth in FY27.
On 11 May 2026, Jindal Stainless announced that its Hisar unit achieved Zero Waste to Landfill certification with a Platinum+ rating.
On May 15, 2026, Jindal Stainless submitted its corporate presentation detailing its operational scale, strategic capex, and market position.
Jindal Stainless reported Q1FY27 results with 10.5% YoY revenue growth to ₹11,278.5 Cr and 7.6% YoY PAT growth to ₹768.7 Cr.
Jindal Stainless filed its FY26 integrated annual report with an unmodified audit opinion, ₹4,204.54 Cr of related-party flows and ₹717.03 Cr of contingent liabilities.

Jindal Stainless' Q1FY27 earnings call kept FY27 volume and ₹18,000-20,000/t H1 EBITDA guidance, reported net debt down to ₹2,950 Cr at 0.53x EBITDA, and flagged PTGMI's shift to associate status from 1 July 2026.

Jindal Stainless' Q1FY27 earnings call kept FY27 volume and ₹18,000-20,000/t EBITDA guidance, reported net debt down to ₹2,950 Cr (0.53x EBITDA) and flagged a gradual volume recovery after a 7.3% YoY sales-volume fall.
Care Ratings upgraded Jindal Stainless' long-term borrowings and NCDs to CARE AA+ (Stable) from CARE AA and reaffirmed the short-term rating at CARE A1+.

Jindal Stainless' August 2026 corporate presentation showed net debt of ₹2,950 Cr EBITDA) at Jun-2026; FY26 revenue of ₹42,955 Cr on 2,566 kt volumes; and an on-going ~₹1,900 Cr HRAP/CRAP and ~₹1,200 Cr Indonesia melt shop expansion.
Jindal Stainless Ltd held its 46th AGM on 2nd September 2026 via VC/OAVM, chaired by **Mr. Ratan Jindal**, approving financial statements, dividend ₹3/share, and re-appointing him as Chairman & MD.

Jindal Stainless Ltd’s 46th AGM (Sept 2, 2026) passed resolutions for standalone/consolidated financial statements, ₹3 dividend, Ratan Jindal’s reappointment, and auditor ratification via remote e-voting.
2026-09-08: JSL Overseas Holding Limited acquired 641,817 shares of Jindal Stainless via open market purchases
2026-09-22: Promoter-group entity JSL Overseas Holding Limited disclosed open-market purchase of 8,61,553 Jindal Stainless shares
2026-09-28: Jindal Stainless fully redeemed 990 listed secured NCDs (ISIN INE220G07127) of ₹10,00,000 face value each at par, a ₹99 Cr outflow.
2026-10-16: Chromeni Steels acquired a 40% stake in Oyster Green Four for ₹1.25 Cr to develop a 24 MW hybrid renewable project.
Q2FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹12,873.86 Cr (+18.2% YoY), net profit ₹897.75 Cr (+11.1% YoY).
Jindal Stainless approved a composite scheme of amalgamation for four wholly owned subsidiaries with an appointed date of April 1, 2027.
2026-10-22: Jindal Stainless reported Q2FY27 net revenue of ₹12,874 Cr, up 18.2% YoY, and approved the amalgamation of four wholly owned subsidiaries.
